The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index:run_end])))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(Html(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index + 1])))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(Html(escape_html(value)))\n                continue\n        nodes.append(Html(escape_html(char)))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n----\n\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and `normalize_label`.\n\nResponsibility: extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes, store them in one\nreference map, and normalize labels with `str.casefold` plus whitespace collapse.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, unescape_and_decode\n\n# A link label may hold at most this many characters between its brackets.\nMAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 999\n# Whitespace inside a label collapses to one space: spaces, tabs and line endings.\nLABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[ \\t\\r\\n]+\")\n# Title delimiters: each opener maps to the closer that ends the title.\nTITLE_CLOSERS = {'\"': '\"', \"'\": \"'\", \"(\": \")\"}\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass LinkReference:\n    \"\"\"A stored definition: the decoded destination and the decoded title, or None when untitled.\"\"\"\n\n    destination: str\n    title: str | None\n\n\ndef normalize_label(label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the matching key for a link label.\n\n    The brackets are stripped when the label has them, the text is case folded, and runs of\n    spaces, tabs and line endings collapse to one space. Matching compares these keys only.\n    \"\"\"\n    if label.startswith(\"[\") and label.endswith(\"]\"):\n        label = label[1:-1]\n    return LABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN.sub(\" \", label.casefold()).strip(\" \")\n\n\nclass ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The document-wide map from normalized label to definition. The first definition wins.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._entries: dict[str, LinkReference] = {}\n\n    def add(self, label: str, destination: str, title: str | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Store a definition under its normalized label unless that label is already present.\"\"\"\n        key = normalize_label(label)\n        if key not in self._entries:\n            self._entries[key] = LinkReference(destination, title)\n\n    def get(self, label: str) -> LinkReference | None:\n        \"\"\"The definition for `label`, matched on its normalized form, or None when absent.\"\"\"\n        return self._entries.get(normalize_label(label))\n\n    def __contains__(self, label: object) -> bool:\n        return isinstance(label, str) and normalize_label(label) in self._entries\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._entries)\n\n\ndef extract_definitions(text: str, references: ReferenceMap) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove the link reference definitions at the start of a closed paragraph's text.\n\n    Each definition found is added to `references`. Scanning stops at the first line that is not a\n    definition, and the rest of the text is returned. Text that is not at the start of the\n    paragraph is never examined, so a definition cannot interrupt a paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    pos = 0\n    while pos < len(text):\n        parsed = _parse_definition(text, pos)\n        if parsed is None:\n            break\n        label, destination, title, pos = parsed\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return text[pos:]\n\n\ndef _parse_definition(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse one definition at `pos`. Return (raw label, destination, title, index after it), or None.\"\"\"\n    label_end = _scan_label(text, pos)\n    if label_end is None:\n        return None\n    label = text[pos:label_end]\n    if text[label_end : label_end + 1] != \":\":\n        return None\n    index = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, label_end + 1)\n    destination = _parse_destination(text, index)\n    if destination is None:\n        return None\n    destination_text, after_destination = destination\n\n    destination_line_end = _line_end(text, after_destination)\n    if not _is_blank(text[after_destination:destination_line_end]):\n        # Anything after the destination on its line must be a title on that same line.\n        title_start = _skip_spaces(text, after_destination)\n        if title_start == after_destination or not _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n            return None\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is None or not _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return None\n        return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n\n    # The destination ends its line. A title may follow on a later line; if it does not parse\n    # cleanly, the definition keeps its destination and the title text stays in the paragraph.\n    title_start = _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text, after_destination)\n    if title_start > after_destination and _is_title_opener(text, title_start):\n        title = _parse_title(text, title_start)\n        if title is not None and _rest_of_line_is_blank(text, title[1]):\n            return label, destination_text, title[0], _after_line(text, title[1])\n    return label, destination_text, None, _after_line(text, destination_line_end)\n\n\ndef _scan_label(text: str, pos: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the closing `]` of a link label at `pos`, or None.\n\n    The label is 1 to 999 characters between its brackets, holds no unescaped bracket, and has at\n    least one non-whitespace character.\n    \"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] != \"[\":\n        return None\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"[\":\n            return None\n        if char == \"]\":\n            inner = text[pos + 1 : index]\n            if not 1 <= len(inner) <= MAX_LABEL_LENGTH or not inner.strip():\n                return None\n            return index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the decoded destination and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"<\":\n        return _parse_angle_destination(text, pos)\n    return _parse_plain_destination(text, pos)\n\n\ndef _parse_angle_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A destination in angle brackets: no line ending, and no unescaped `<` or `>` inside.\"\"\"\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char in \"<\\n\":\n            return None\n        if char == \">\":\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _parse_plain_destination(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A nonempty destination with no space or control character and balanced parentheses.\"\"\"\n    index = pos\n    depth = 0\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == \"(\":\n            depth += 1\n        elif char == \")\":\n            if depth == 0:\n                break\n            depth -= 1\n        elif char == \" \" or _is_ascii_control(char):\n            break\n        index += 1\n    if index == pos or depth != 0:\n        return None\n    return unescape_and_decode(text[pos:index]), index\n\n\ndef _parse_title(text: str, pos: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"A title in double quotes, single quotes or parentheses. Return (decoded title, index past it).\"\"\"\n    opener = text[pos]\n    closer = TITLE_CLOSERS[opener]\n    index = pos + 1\n    while index < len(text):\n        char = text[index]\n        if char == \"\\\\\" and _is_escapable(text, index):\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        if char == closer:\n            return unescape_and_decode(text[pos + 1 : index]), index + 1\n        if opener == \"(\" and char == \"(\":\n            return None\n        index += 1\n    return None\n\n\ndef _is_escapable(text: str, index: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the backslash at `index` escapes the character after it.\"\"\"\n    return index + 1 < len(text) and text[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION\n\n\ndef _is_title_opener(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return text[pos : pos + 1] in TITLE_CLOSERS\n\n\ndef _is_ascii_control(char: str) -> bool:\n    return char < \" \" or char == \"\\x7f\"\n\n\ndef _is_blank(segment: str) -> bool:\n    return segment.strip(\" \\t\") == \"\"\n\n\ndef _skip_spaces(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after `pos` that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n    while pos < len(text) and text[pos] in \" \\t\":\n        pos += 1\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _skip_whitespace_with_line_ending(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs, then at most one line ending, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos)\n    if text[pos : pos + 1] == \"\\n\":\n        pos = _skip_spaces(text, pos + 1)\n    return pos\n\n\ndef _line_end(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index of the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = text.find(\"\\n\", pos)\n    return len(text) if end == -1 else end\n\n\ndef _after_line(text: str, pos: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the line ending at or after `pos`, or the end of the text.\"\"\"\n    end = _line_end(text, pos)\n    return min(end + 1, len(text))\n\n\ndef _rest_of_line_is_blank(text: str, pos: int) -> bool:\n    return _is_blank(text[pos : _line_end(text, pos)])\n----\n\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n----\n\"\"\"Character references and backslash escapes.\n\nResponsibility: decode named entities (from the standard library table `html.entities.html5`,\nnames ending in a semicolon only) and numeric character references, and provide the backslash\nunescape helper and the shared destination, title and info-string helper.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport html.entities\nimport re\nimport string\n\n# The ASCII punctuation characters that a backslash may escape.\nASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset(string.punctuation)\n\n# A named reference: `&`, a name, then `;`. The table lookup adds the semicolon back.\nNAMED_REFERENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"&([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*);\")\n# A decimal reference has 1 to 7 digits. Zero, surrogates and out-of-range values\n    become U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    if code_point == 0 or code_point > MAX_CODE_POINT or 0xD800 <= code_point <= 0xDFFF:\n        return REPLACEMENT_CHARAC","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false,"persistedOutputPath":"/home/barlo/.drydock/claude-home/projects/-mnt-c-Users-barlo-projects-drydock-uat-CommonMark-runs-20261014-053711-build-commonmark/60a1f7ba-5e9e-43f0-811c-26aa370c7215/tool-results/bmrpkrpum.txt","persistedOutputSize":31700},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01UmDptvqaiSa1YZsGywp8AC","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LtADK259RECXqd2sYTdNBw","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\n4\tdelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\n5\tfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\t\n8\timport re\n9\timport unicodedata\n10\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n11\t\n12\tfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\n13\tfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n14\t\n15\t# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n16\t# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n17\t\n18\t\n19\t@dataclass\n20\tclass Text:\n21\t    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n22\t\n23\t    literal: str\n24\t\n25\t\n26\t@dataclass\n27\tclass Html:\n28\t    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n29\t\n30\t    html: str\n31\t\n32\t\n33\t@dataclass\n34\tclass Element:\n35\t    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n36\t\n37\t    tag: str\n38\t    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n39\t\n40\t\n41\tNode = Text | Html | Element\n42\t\n43\t\n44\t@dataclass(eq=False)\n45\tclass Delimiter:\n46\t    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n47\t\n48\t    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n49\t    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n50\t    \"\"\"\n51\t\n52\t    node: Text | None\n53\t    char: str\n54\t    length: int\n55\t    original_length: int\n56\t    can_open: bool\n57\t    can_close: bool\n58\t    active: bool = True\n59\t    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n60\t    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n61\t\n62\t# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n63\t# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\n64\tAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n65\t# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\n66\tURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n67\t# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\n68\tEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n69\t    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n70\t    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n71\t    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n72\t)\n73\t\n74\t# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\n75\tBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n76\t\n77\t# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n78\t_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n79\t# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n80\t_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n81\t_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n82\t_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n83\t# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n84\t_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n85\t_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n86\t_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n87\t# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\n88\tRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n89\t    re.compile(pattern)\n90\t    for pattern in (\n91\t        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n92\t        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n93\t        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n94\t        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n95\t        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n96\t        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n97\t        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n98\t    )\n99\t)\n100\t\n101\t\n102\tdef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n103\t    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n104\t\n105\t    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n106\t    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n107\t    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n108\t    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n109\t    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n110\t    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n111\t    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n112\t    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n113\t    pairs into emphasis. Everything else is escaped text.\n114\t    \"\"\"\n115\t    nodes: list[Node] = []\n116\t    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n117\t    index = 0\n118\t    while index < len(raw):\n119\t        char = raw[index]\n120\t        if char == \"`\":\n121\t            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n122\t            if code_span is not None:\n123\t                html, index = code_span\n124\t                nodes.append(Html(html))\n125\t                continue\n126\t            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n127\t            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index:run_end])))\n128\t            index = run_end\n129\t            continue\n130\t        if char == \"<\":\n131\t            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n132\t            if autolink is not None:\n133\t                html, index = autolink\n134\t                nodes.append(Html(html))\n135\t                continue\n136\t            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n137\t            if raw_html_end is not None:\n138\t                nodes.append(Html(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n139\t                index = raw_html_end\n140\t                continue\n141\t        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n142\t            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index + 1])))\n143\t            index += 2\n144\t            continue\n145\t        elif char in \"*_\":\n146\t            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n147\t            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n148\t            index = run_end\n149\t            continue\n150\t        elif char == \"&\":\n151\t            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n152\t            if reference is not None:\n153\t                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n154\t                value, index = reference\n155\t                nodes.append(Html(escape_html(value)))\n156\t                continue\n157\t        nodes.append(Html(escape_html(char)))\n158\t        index += 1\n159\t    stack.process_emphasis()\n160\t    return render_nodes(nodes)\n161\t\n162\t\n163\tdef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n164\t    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n165\t    parts: list[str] = []\n166\t    for node in nodes:\n167\t        if isinstance(node, Html):\n168\t            parts.append(node.html)\n169\t        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n170\t            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n171\t        else:\n172\t            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n173\t    return \"\".join(parts)\n174\t\n175\t\n176\tdef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n177\t    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n178\t    end = start + 1\n179\t    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n180\t        end += 1\n181\t    return end\n182\t\n183\t\n184\tdef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n185\t    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n186\t\n187\t    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n188\t    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n189\t    \"\"\"\n190\t    char = raw[start]\n191\t    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n192\t    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n193\t    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n194\t    if char == \"*\":\n195\t        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n196\t    else:\n197\t        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n198\t        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n199\t    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n200\t\n201\t\n202\tdef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n203\t    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n204\t\n205\t    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n206\t    \"\"\"\n207\t    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n208\t\n209\t\n210\tdef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n211\t    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n212\t    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n213\t\n214\t\n215\tdef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n216\t    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n217\t    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n218\t        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n219\t    )\n220\t    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n221\t        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n222\t    )\n223\t    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n224\t\n225\t\n226\tclass DelimiterStack:\n227\t    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n228\t\n229\t    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n230\t    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n231\t    sibling of the others in that list.\n232\t    \"\"\"\n233\t\n234\t    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n235\t        self.nodes = nodes\n236\t        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n237\t        self.top = self.bottom\n238\t\n239\t    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n240\t        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n241\t        self.nodes.append(node)\n242\t        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n243\t        self.top.next = entry\n244\t        self.top = entry\n245\t\n246\t    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n247\t        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n248\t\n249\t        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n250\t        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n251\t        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n252\t        \"\"\"\n253\t        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n254\t        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n255\t        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n256\t        while closer is not None:\n257\t            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n258\t            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n259\t            if opener is None:\n260\t                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n261\t                following = closer.next\n262\t                if not closer.can_open:\n263\t                    self._unlink(closer)\n264\t                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n265\t                continue\n266\t            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n267\t            used = 2 if strong else 1\n268\t            opener.length -= used\n269\t            closer.length -= used\n270\t            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n271\t            self._sync_literal(opener)\n272\t            self._sync_literal(closer)\n273\t            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n274\t            if opener.length == 0:\n275\t                self._drop(opener)\n276\t            if closer.length == 0:\n277\t                following = closer.next\n278\t                self._drop(closer)\n279\t                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n280\t        bottom.next = None\n281\t        self.top = bottom\n282\t\n283\t    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n284\t        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n285\t            entry = entry.next\n286\t        return entry\n287\t\n288\t    def _find_opener(\n289\t        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n290\t    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n291\t        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n292\t\n293\t        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n294\t        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n295\t        \"\"\"\n296\t        potential = closer.previous\n297\t        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n298\t            odd_match = (\n299\t                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n300\t                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n301\t                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n302\t            )\n303\t            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n304\t                return potential\n305\t            potential = potential.previous\n306\t        return None\n307\t\n308\t    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n309\t        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n310\t        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n311\t        if entry.next is not None:\n312\t            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n313\t        else:\n314\t            self.top = entry.previous\n315\t\n316\t    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n317\t        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n318\t        opener.next = closer\n319\t        closer.previous = opener\n320\t\n321\t    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n322\t        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n323\t        self._unlink(entry)\n324\t        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n325\t\n326\t    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n327\t        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n328\t\n329\t    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n330\t        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n331\t        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n332\t        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n333\t        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n334\t\n335\t    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n336\t        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n337\t            if candidate is node:\n338\t                return index\n339\t        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n340\t\n341\t\n342\tdef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n343\t    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n344\t\n345\t    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n346\t    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n347\t    \"\"\"\n348\t    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n349\t    width = len(opener.group())\n350\t    content_start = opener.end()\n351\t    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n352\t        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n353\t            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n354\t            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n355\t    return None\n356\t\n357\t\n358\tdef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n359\t    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n360\t\n361\t    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n362\t    \"\"\"\n363\t    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n364\t    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n365\t        return text[1:-1]\n366\t    return text\n367\t\n368\t\n369\tdef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n370\t    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n371\t    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n372\t    if match is None:\n373\t        return None\n374\t    body = match.group(1)\n375\t    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n376\t        href = body\n377\t    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n378\t        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n379\t    else:\n380\t        return None\n381\t    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n382\t\n383\t\n384\tdef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n385\t    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n386\t    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n387\t        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n388\t        if match is not None:\n389\t            return match.end()\n390\t    return None\n391\t\n392\t\n393\tdef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n394\t    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n395\t    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n396\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"60a1f7ba-5e9e-43f0-811c-26aa370c7215","uuid":"ad3d01d0-9721-49dc-89ff-e15296dc439b","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:32:54.726Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/inlines.py","content":"\"\"\"Phase 2: inline parsing.\n\nResponsibility: parse the raw text of paragraphs and headings into inline nodes with the\ndelimiter-stack algorithms (look for link or image, process emphasis), using the reference map\nfrom `mdparser.refs`.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, match_reference\nfrom mdparser.render import escape_html, percent_encode_url\n\n# Inline nodes. A delimiter run is a `Text` node until emphasis consumes some of its characters;\n# whatever is left over is literal text. Everything else is already-rendered `Html`.\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Text:\n    \"\"\"An unconsumed run of `*` or `_` characters, escaped on output.\"\"\"\n\n    literal: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Html:\n    \"\"\"Rendered inline HTML: text, a code span, an autolink, raw HTML, or a decoded reference.\"\"\"\n\n    html: str\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Element:\n    \"\"\"An emphasis element. Its children are the nodes that sat between its opener and closer.\"\"\"\n\n    tag: str\n    children: list[\"Node\"] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\nNode = Text | Html | Element\n\n\n@dataclass(eq=False)\nclass Delimiter:\n    \"\"\"A delimiter stack entry. Identity matters, so entries compare by object, not by value.\n\n    `previous` and `next` link the stack from the bottom sentinel upward. `node` is the `Text` node\n    holding the run, or None for the bottom sentinel.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    node: Text | None\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    original_length: int\n    can_open: bool\n    can_close: bool\n    active: bool = True\n    previous: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n    next: \"Delimiter | None\" = None\n\n# The body of an autolink: everything between `<` and `>` except ASCII control characters, space,\n# `<` and `>`. The URI and email rules are checked against this body.\nAUTOLINK_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"<([^\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]*)>\")\n# A scheme is 2 to 32 characters: an ASCII letter, then letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`.\nURI_SCHEME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]{1,31}:\")\n# The non-normative HTML5 email address regex from the spec, without its anchors.\nEMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+\"\n    r\"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\"\n    r\"(?:\\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*\"\n)\n\n# A backtick string is a maximal run of backticks. Code spans open and close on equal-length runs.\nBACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"`+\")\n\n# Whitespace in a raw HTML tag: spaces and tabs, with at most one line ending.\n_WS = r\"[ \\t]*(?:\\n[ \\t]*)?\"\n# Whitespace that must be present: an attribute cannot follow its tag name or value directly.\n_WS_REQUIRED = r\"(?=[ \\t\\n])\" + _WS\n_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n_ATTR_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n# An unquoted value is nonempty and has no whitespace, quote, `=`, `<`, `>` or backtick.\n_UNQUOTED_VALUE = r\"[^ \\t\\n\\r\\\"'=<>`]+\"\n_ATTR_VALUE = rf\"(?:{_UNQUOTED_VALUE}|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\")\"\n_ATTRIBUTE = rf\"{_WS_REQUIRED}{_ATTR_NAME}(?:{_WS}={_WS}{_ATTR_VALUE})?\"\n# The raw HTML grammars from the spec, tried in order. Each one is anchored at the `<` by `match`.\nRAW_HTML_PATTERNS = tuple(\n    re.compile(pattern)\n    for pattern in (\n        rf\"<{_TAG_NAME}(?:{_ATTRIBUTE})*{_WS}/?>\",\n        rf\"</{_TAG_NAME}{_WS}>\",\n        # `<!-->` and `<!--->` are complete comments; any other comment ends at the first `-->`.\n        r\"<!--(?:>|->|(?s:.*?)-->)\",\n        r\"<\\?(?s:.*?)\\?>\",\n        r\"<![A-Za-z][^>]*>\",\n        r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[(?s:.*?)\\]\\]>\",\n    )\n)\n\n\ndef parse_inline(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Inline parser hook: return the HTML for a block's raw content.\n\n    The scan runs left to right. At each special character the constructs that start there are\n    tried, and the first one that matches is taken whole. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML have\n    equal precedence, so whichever starts first wins. A backtick string with no closing run of the\n    same length is literal text, and the whole run is consumed. An autolink or raw HTML tag is taken\n    whole, so a backslash inside it stays literal. A backslash before ASCII punctuation yields that\n    character, so `\\\\<` and `\\\\`` do not open a construct. A recognized character reference is\n    decoded and its character is escaped text, so `&#42;` never opens structure. A run of `*` or `_`\n    becomes a delimiter run: a text node pushed on the delimiter stack, which process_emphasis then\n    pairs into emphasis. Everything else is escaped text.\n    \"\"\"\n    nodes: list[Node] = []\n    stack = DelimiterStack(nodes)\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(raw):\n        char = raw[index]\n        if char == \"`\":\n            code_span = _match_code_span(raw, index)\n            if code_span is not None:\n                html, index = code_span\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            run_end = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, index).end()\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index:run_end])))\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        if char == \"<\":\n            autolink = _match_autolink(raw, index)\n            if autolink is not None:\n                html, index = autolink\n                nodes.append(Html(html))\n                continue\n            raw_html_end = _match_raw_html(raw, index)\n            if raw_html_end is not None:\n                nodes.append(Html(raw[index:raw_html_end]))\n                index = raw_html_end\n                continue\n        elif char == \"\\\\\" and index + 1 < len(raw) and raw[index + 1] in ASCII_PUNCTUATION:\n            nodes.append(Html(escape_html(raw[index + 1])))\n            index += 2\n            continue\n        elif char in \"*_\":\n            run_end = _delimiter_run_end(raw, index)\n            _push_delimiter_run(stack, raw, index, run_end)\n            index = run_end\n            continue\n        elif char == \"&\":\n            reference = match_reference(raw, index)\n            if reference is not None:\n                # A decoded character is text, so it is escaped like any other text.\n                value, index = reference\n                nodes.append(Html(escape_html(value)))\n                continue\n        nodes.append(Html(escape_html(char)))\n        index += 1\n    stack.process_emphasis()\n    return render_nodes(nodes)\n\n\ndef render_nodes(nodes: list[Node]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a node list to HTML. Leftover delimiter runs are escaped literal text.\"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for node in nodes:\n        if isinstance(node, Html):\n            parts.append(node.html)\n        elif isinstance(node, Text):\n            parts.append(escape_html(node.literal))\n        else:\n            parts.append(f\"<{node.tag}>{render_nodes(node.children)}</{node.tag}>\")\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _delimiter_run_end(raw: str, start: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the maximal run of the delimiter character at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start + 1\n    while end < len(raw) and raw[end] == raw[start]:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _push_delimiter_run(stack: \"DelimiterStack\", raw: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append the run raw[start:end] as a text node and push its stack entry with flanking flags.\n\n    The characters before and after the run decide flanking. The start and end of the line count\n    as whitespace, so a missing neighbour is passed as None.\n    \"\"\"\n    char = raw[start]\n    before = raw[start - 1] if start > 0 else None\n    after = raw[end] if end < len(raw) else None\n    left_flanking, right_flanking = _flanking(before, after)\n    if char == \"*\":\n        can_open, can_close = left_flanking, right_flanking\n    else:\n        can_open = left_flanking and (not right_flanking or _is_punctuation(before))\n        can_close = right_flanking and (not left_flanking or _is_punctuation(after))\n    stack.push(Text(char * (end - start)), char, end - start, can_open, can_close)\n\n\ndef _is_whitespace(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode whitespace: tab, line feed, form feed, carriage return, or a Zs character.\n\n    The start and end of the line are passed as None and count as whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return char is None or char in \"\\t\\n\\f\\r\" or unicodedata.category(char) == \"Zs\"\n\n\ndef _is_punctuation(char: str | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Unicode punctuation or symbol: categories P* and S*. None (the line edge) is not one.\"\"\"\n    return char is not None and unicodedata.category(char)[0] in \"PS\"\n\n\ndef _flanking(before: str | None, after: str | None) -> tuple[bool, bool]:\n    \"\"\"Return (left-flanking, right-flanking) for a delimiter run with these neighbours.\"\"\"\n    left_flanking = not _is_whitespace(after) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(after) or _is_whitespace(before) or _is_punctuation(before)\n    )\n    right_flanking = not _is_whitespace(before) and (\n        not _is_punctuation(before) or _is_whitespace(after) or _is_punctuation(after)\n    )\n    return left_flanking, right_flanking\n\n\nclass DelimiterStack:\n    \"\"\"The delimiter stack: a doubly linked list of `Delimiter` entries over a sibling node list.\n\n    The bottom sentinel is never removed, so `stack_bottom` is always an entry. `process_emphasis`\n    wraps the nodes between a matched pair inside `nodes`, so every delimiter it touches must be a\n    sibling of the others in that list.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, nodes: list[Node]) -> None:\n        self.nodes = nodes\n        self.bottom = Delimiter(None, \"\", 0, 0, False, False)\n        self.top = self.bottom\n\n    def push(self, node: Text, char: str, length: int, can_open: bool, can_close: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a delimiter entry for a run that is already a `Text` node in `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self.nodes.append(node)\n        entry = Delimiter(node, char, length, length, can_open, can_close, previous=self.top)\n        self.top.next = entry\n        self.top = entry\n\n    def process_emphasis(self, stack_bottom: Delimiter | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pair delimiter runs above `stack_bottom` into em and strong (Appendix algorithm).\n\n        `openers_bottom` is keyed by delimiter character, the closer's original length mod 3, and\n        whether the closer can also open. Each key holds the lowest entry an opener search may\n        reach, so a failed search is not repeated. Unmatched runs stay as literal text.\n        \"\"\"\n        bottom = self.bottom if stack_bottom is None else stack_bottom\n        openers_bottom: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Delimiter] = {}\n        closer = self._first_closer(bottom.next)\n        while closer is not None:\n            key = (closer.char, closer.original_length % 3, closer.can_open)\n            opener = self._find_opener(closer, bottom, openers_bottom.get(key, bottom))\n            if opener is None:\n                openers_bottom[key] = closer.previous\n                following = closer.next\n                if not closer.can_open:\n                    self._unlink(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n                continue\n            strong = opener.length >= 2 and closer.length >= 2\n            used = 2 if strong else 1\n            opener.length -= used\n            closer.length -= used\n            self._unlink_between(opener, closer)\n            self._sync_literal(opener)\n            self._sync_literal(closer)\n            self._wrap(opener.node, closer.node, \"strong\" if strong else \"em\")\n            if opener.length == 0:\n                self._drop(opener)\n            if closer.length == 0:\n                following = closer.next\n                self._drop(closer)\n                closer = self._first_closer(following)\n        bottom.next = None\n        self.top = bottom\n\n    def _first_closer(self, entry: Delimiter | None) -> Delimiter | None:\n        while entry is not None and not entry.can_close:\n            entry = entry.next\n        return entry\n\n    def _find_opener(\n        self, closer: Delimiter, bottom: Delimiter, openers_bottom: Delimiter\n    ) -> Delimiter | None:\n        \"\"\"Search back from the closer for a matching opener above both lower bounds, or None.\n\n        Under the multiple-of-3 rule a pair is skipped when one run can both open and close and the\n        original lengths sum to a multiple of 3, unless both lengths are multiples of 3.\n        \"\"\"\n        potential = closer.previous\n        while potential is not None and potential is not bottom and potential is not openers_bottom:\n            odd_match = (\n                (closer.can_open or potential.can_close)\n                and closer.original_length % 3 != 0\n                and (potential.original_length + closer.original_length) % 3 == 0\n            )\n            if potential.char == closer.char and potential.can_open and not odd_match:\n                return potential\n            potential = potential.previous\n        return None\n\n    def _unlink(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an entry from the stack. Its node stays in `nodes` as text.\"\"\"\n        entry.previous.next = entry.next\n        if entry.next is not None:\n            entry.next.previous = entry.previous\n        else:\n            self.top = entry.previous\n\n    def _unlink_between(self, opener: Delimiter, closer: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove every entry strictly between an opener and a closer from the stack.\"\"\"\n        opener.next = closer\n        closer.previous = opener\n\n    def _drop(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove an exhausted run from the stack and from `nodes`.\"\"\"\n        self._unlink(entry)\n        del self.nodes[self._index_of(entry.node)]\n\n    def _sync_literal(self, entry: Delimiter) -> None:\n        entry.node.literal = entry.char * entry.length\n\n    def _wrap(self, opener_node: Text, closer_node: Text, tag: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the nodes between opener and closer into a new element after the opener.\"\"\"\n        start = self._index_of(opener_node) + 1\n        end = self._index_of(closer_node)\n        self.nodes[start:end] = [Element(tag, self.nodes[start:end])]\n\n    def _index_of(self, node: Node) -> int:\n        for index, candidate in enumerate(self.nodes):\n            if candidate is node:\n                return index\n        raise ValueError(\"delimiter node is not in the node list\")\n\n\ndef _match_code_span(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the code span HTML for a backtick string at `start` and the index just past it.\n\n    The span closes at the next backtick string of exactly the same length. Returns None when no\n    such closing run exists, so the opening run is literal text.\n    \"\"\"\n    opener = BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    width = len(opener.group())\n    content_start = opener.end()\n    for closer in BACKTICK_RUN_PATTERN.finditer(raw, content_start):\n        if len(closer.group()) == width:\n            content = _normalize_code_content(raw[content_start : closer.start()])\n            return f\"<code>{escape_html(content)}</code>\", closer.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _normalize_code_content(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Turn line endings into spaces, then strip one space from each end when both ends are spaces.\n\n    Stripping is skipped when the content is entirely spaces. Only U+0020 counts as a space.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == \" \" and text[-1] == \" \" and text.strip(\" \"):\n        return text[1:-1]\n    return text\n\n\ndef _match_autolink(raw: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the link HTML for an autolink at `start` and the index just past it, or None.\"\"\"\n    match = AUTOLINK_PATTERN.match(raw, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    body = match.group(1)\n    if URI_SCHEME_PATTERN.match(body):\n        href = body\n    elif EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(body):\n        href = \"mailto:\" + body\n    else:\n        return None\n    return _link_html(href, body), match.end()\n\n\ndef _match_raw_html(raw: str, start: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the index just past the raw HTML construct at `start`, or None if none matches.\"\"\"\n    for pattern in RAW_HTML_PATTERNS:\n        match = pattern.match(raw, start)\n        if match is not None:\n            return match.end()\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_html(href: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a link: the href is percent-encoded then escaped; the label is escaped text.\"\"\"\n    return f'<a href=\"{escape_html(percent_encode_url(href))}\">{escape_html(text)}</a>'\n","numLines":396,"startLine":1,"totalLines":396}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01LtADK259RECXqd2sYTdNBw","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016BpjBUNCtzyMi7UhcXTza6","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Link reference definitions: extraction, the document-wide reference map, and `normalize_label`.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes, store them in one\n4\treference map, and normalize labels with `str.casefold` plus whitespace collapse.\n5\t\"\"\"\n6\t\n7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n8\t\n9\timport re\n10\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n11\t\n12\tfrom mdparser.entities import ASCII_PUNCTUATION, unescape_and_decode\n13\t\n14\t# A link label may hold at most this many characters between its brackets.\n15\tMAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 999\n16\t# Whitespace inside a label collapses to one space: spaces, tabs and line endings.\n17\tLABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[ \\t\\r\\n]+\")\n18\t# Title delimiters: each opener maps to the closer that ends the title.\n19\tTITLE_CLOSERS = {'\"': '\"', \"'\": \"'\", \"(\": \")\"}\n20\t\n21\t\n22\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n23\tclass LinkReference:\n24\t    \"\"\"A stored definition: the decoded destination and the decoded title, or None when untitled.\"\"\"\n25\t\n26\t    destination: str\n27\t    title: str | None\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tdef normalize_label(label: str) -> str:\n31\t    \"\"\"Return the matching key for a link label.\n32\t\n33\t    The brackets are stripped when the label has them, the text is case folded, and runs of\n34\t    spaces, tabs and line endings collapse to one space. Matching compares these keys only.\n35\t    \"\"\"\n36\t    if label.startswith(\"[\") and label.endswith(\"]\"):\n37\t        label = label[1:-1]\n38\t    return LABEL_WHITESPACE_PATTERN.sub(\" \", label.casefold()).strip(\" \")\n39\t\n40\t\n41\tclass ReferenceMap:\n42\t    \"\"\"The document-wide map from normalized label to definition. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\n5\tentities must match the spec examples.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\t\n8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t\n10\timport string\n11\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n12\t\n13\tfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n14\t\n15\tInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n16\t\n17\tESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\n18\tURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\n19\tHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n20\t\n21\t\n22\tdef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n23\t    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n24\t    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n25\t        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n26\t    return text\n27\t\n28\t\n29\tdef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n30\t    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n31\t\n32\t    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n33\t    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n34\t    \"\"\"\n35\t    out: list[str] = []\n36\t    index = 0\n37\t    while index < len(url):\n38\t        char = url[index]\n39\t        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n40\t            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n41\t            index += 3\n42\t            continue\n43\t        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n44\t            out.append(char)\n45\t        else:\n46\t            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n47\t        index += 1\n48\t    return \"\".join(out)\n49\t\n50\t\n51\tdef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n52\t    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n56\t    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n57\t\n58\t    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n59\t    returns that content's HTML.\n60\t    \"\"\"\n61\t    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n62\t\n63\t\n64\tdef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n65\t    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n66\t        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n67\t    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n68\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"60a1f7ba-5e9e-43f0-811c-26aa370c7215","uuid":"896e83ad-614d-48c3-acb5-6a30894326f8","timestamp":"2026-10-14T06:32:55.286Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","content":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n","numLines":68,"startLine":1,"totalLines":68}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Ro9HyaaqDdcoaemwe7RAh9","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
